DPF replacement cost overview What Does DPF Replacement Cost in the UK? For most UK diesel drivers, DPF issues are common and often misunderstood. Here's what you can expect: DPF cleaning (off-car) £180–£400 Most effective method DPF cleaning (postal) £180–£400 Post your DPF for cleaning Forced regeneration £85–£300 Diagnostic equipment required DPF replacement (compact) £800–£1,500 Fiesta, Corsa, Polo, Clio DPF replacement (family) £1,500–£2,500 Focus, Golf, A3, Astra DPF replacement (SUV/4x4) £2,500–£3,500+ Range Rover, Q7, X5 [EM-QUOTE] These figures are derived from supplier quotes submitted through our platform. Prices are ex VAT and assume independent specialist labour. Main dealer costs are typically 40-60% higher. Prices are ex VAT and assume independent specialist labour. Cleaning vs replacement Cleaning vs Replacement — The Decision Most issues can be resolved with cleaning. Replacement is only needed when the filter is physically damaged. ✔ When cleaning works Clogged with soot £150–£400 The DPF needs regeneration — cleaning removes the soot and restores function. Clogged with ash £150–£400 Ash builds up over time — professional cleaning removes the ash. Excessive back-pressure £150–£400 Cleaning reduces back-pressure to normal levels. Most DPF issues (90%+) £150–£400 Cleaning resolves the problem in the vast majority of cases. ⚠️ When replacement is needed Cracked filter £800–£3,500+ Physical damage — cleaning can't fix cracks. Replacement required. Melted filter £800–£3,500+ The substrate has melted — cleaning can't fix it. Replacement required. Missing substrate £800–£3,500+ The filter has disintegrated — replacement required. Approximately 5–10% of cases £800–£3,500+ Replacement is actually needed. Always try cleaning first. ⭐ The rule of thumb: Always try cleaning first. Replacement costs £800–£3,500+, while cleaning costs £150–£400. In the vast majority of cases, cleaning restores the filter to near-new condition. DPF cleaning options Understanding Your Cleaning Choices Different cleaning methods suit different levels of clogging. Here's what each option involves. Option Cost Timeline Best For Forced regeneration £85–£300 Same day Mild clogging — filter can still regenerate Off-car cleaning £180–£400 1–2 days Moderate to severe clogging Postal cleaning £180–£400 3–5 days When you can't drive to a specialist On-car cleaning (chemical) £150–£300 Same day Mild to moderate clogging — less effective [EM-QUOTE] Derived from supplier quotes. Prices are ex VAT. Signs of DPF failure How to Spot DPF Problems Early detection can save you hundreds. Here are the most common symptoms and what they mean. Symptom What It Means Urgency Action DPF warning light Filter is clogged — needs regeneration ⚠️ Medium Drive at 40mph+ for 15-20 mins to regenerate Reduced power / limp mode DPF severely clogged — ECU limits power ⚠️⚠️ HIGH Stop driving — professional clean required Increased fuel consumption Engine working harder to push exhaust through DPF ⚠️ Medium Have it checked — cleaning likely needed Excessive smoke (black) DPF not regenerating — soot building up ⚠️ Medium-High Have it checked — cleaning may resolve Rough idle / misfire DPF back-pressure causing engine issues ⚠️ Medium-High Have it checked immediately Engine management light DPF-related fault codes ⚠️ Medium Diagnostic check required Regeneration frequency DPF regenerating more often than normal ⚠️ Medium Underlying issue — faulty sensor/EGR/injector [EM-QUOTE] Based on specialist interviews and customer submissions. Causes of DPF failure Why DPFs Fail Understanding the root cause helps you prevent future issues. 🚗 Short journeys DPF can't regenerate because exhaust doesn't get hot enough. The filter never reaches 600°C+ to burn off soot. ✔ Prevention: Regular longer journeys (40mph+ for 20 mins) 🔧 Faulty EGR valve EGR recirculates exhaust gases — adds soot to DPF, accelerating clogging. ✔ Prevention: Regular maintenance, EGR cleaning 💉 Faulty injectors Over-fuelling creates more soot, clogging the DPF faster. ✔ Prevention: Regular maintenance, injector cleaning 🛢️ Oil ash accumulation Oil ash builds up over time — can't be regenerated away. Requires professional cleaning. ✔ Prevention: Regular DPF cleaning (every 30,000–40,000 miles) 📡 Faulty sensors Pressure/temperature sensors fail — ECU doesn't know when to regenerate. ✔ Prevention: Regular diagnostics, faulty sensor replacement ⛽ Low engine oil level Over-filling or low oil can cause DPF issues. Use the correct oil spec. ✔ Prevention: Regular oil checks, correct oil spec (ACEA C1/C2/C3) 💡 Why short journeys cause DPF problems: For the DPF to regenerate, the exhaust must reach 600°C+ . This requires sustained driving at 40mph+ for 15-20 minutes . If you only do short journeys, the DPF never gets hot enough — soot accumulates and the DPF clogs. Prevention The DPF Prevention Plan Follow these simple steps to keep your DPF healthy and avoid costly replacements. 1. Drive 40mph+ for 20 minutes weekly Especially if you only do short journeys. This allows the DPF to regenerate naturally. 2. Use the correct engine oil Low-ash oil (ACEA C1/C2/C3) reduces ash accumulation in the DPF. 3. Don't overfill engine oil Overfilling can cause DPF problems. Check your oil level regularly. 4. Regular maintenance EGR, injectors, sensors — keep them in good condition to prevent DPF issues. 5. Regular DPF cleaning Every 30,000–40,000 miles. Professional cleaning removes ash that regeneration can't clear. ⚠️ Illegal option — DO NOT DO THIS DPF Delete — The Illegal Option Why you should NEVER remove a DPF ❌ Legality ILLEGAL — punishable by MOT failure and fines up to £1,000 (cars) or £2,500 (vans). ❌ MOT Will FAIL emissions testing. Automatic MOT failure since 2018. ❌ Insurance Your insurance is void — you're driving uninsured. Claims will be rejected. ❌ Environment Significantly increased emissions — visible black smoke, particulate matter, NOx. ⚠️ Never use a DPF delete service. It's illegal, environmentally damaging, and will cause you problems with MOT, insurance, and potentially the police. The short-term saving is not worth it. What's included — and what's not Know Exactly What You're Paying For When you pay for DPF cleaning or replacement, here's what's typically included and what's extra. ✔ Typically included 🔧 DPF removal Removing the DPF from the vehicle (off-car clean). 🧼 Professional cleaning Specialist cleaning machine — removes soot and ash. 🔄 DPF refitting Refitting the cleaned DPF to the vehicle. 📋 Testing Running the engine, checking for DPF pressure. 🛠️ Diagnostic reset Resetting DPF fault codes after service. ⚠️ Typically NOT included (extra cost) 🔄 DPF replacement Only needed if cracked or melted. Extra £800–£3,500+. 🔧 EGR valve cleaning Often needed as part of DPF solution. Extra £100–£300. 💉 Injector cleaning Over-fuelling contributes to DPF issues. Extra £80–£200. 📡 Pressure sensor Faulty sensor may have caused DPF issue. Extra £50–£150. 🌡️ Temperature sensor Faulty sensor may have caused DPF issue. Extra £50–£150. 🔍 DPF pressure pipe cleaning Often blocked — causes sensor issues. Extra £20–£50. Always ask your supplier for a full written breakdown before agreeing to any work. Before you agree 10 Questions to Ask Before DPF Service Asking the right questions can save you hundreds and prevent unnecessary replacement. Here's a checklist specific to DPF issues. 1. Is cleaning possible or do I need replacement? In most cases, cleaning resolves the issue. Replacement is only needed if cracked, melted, or severely damaged. 2. What's included in the cleaning price? Get a full written breakdown: removal, cleaning, refitting, testing, and diagnostic reset. 3. What cleaning method do you use? Off-car cleaning (best), forced regeneration (mild issues), or chemical (less effective). 4. What's the condition of my DPF? Ask for an inspection report. Is it clogged with soot, ash, or physically damaged? 5. What warranty do you offer on the cleaning? Typical warranty is 6–12 months on the cleaning work. Get it in writing. 6. What's the root cause of the DPF issue? Short journeys, faulty EGR, faulty injectors, or something else? Address the root cause. 7. What's the timeline from booking to completion? Off-car cleaning: 1-2 days. Forced regeneration: a few hours. Replacement: 2-3 days. 8. Is there any diagnostic work included? Ask if fault code reading and DPF pressure measurement are included in the price. 9. Do you have experience with my vehicle/engine type? Some engines have known DPF issues. Ask about their experience. 10. Can you provide a written quote? Get everything in writing: scope of work, cost, timeline, and warranty terms. Frequently asked questions Common Questions About DPF Replacement & Cleaning How much does DPF replacement cost in the UK? + DPF replacement costs range from £800 to £3,500+ depending on vehicle. Compact cars cost £800-£1,500, family cars £1,500-£2,500, and SUVs/commercial vehicles £2,500-£3,500+. However, cleaning (£150-£400) resolves most issues — replacement is only needed when the filter is physically cracked or melted. Can I clean a DPF instead of replacing it? + Yes — in most cases, cleaning resolves the issue. Off-car professional cleaning (£180-£400) restores the filter to near-new condition. Replacement (£800-£3,500+) is only needed if the DPF is cracked, melted, or structurally damaged. Always try cleaning first. What are the signs of a clogged DPF? + DPF warning light, reduced power / limp mode, increased fuel consumption, excessive black smoke, rough idle, engine management light, and frequent regeneration. The DPF warning light is the most common early sign. Can I drive with a DPF warning light? + If the DPF warning light is on, drive at 40mph+ for 15-20 minutes to allow the filter to regenerate. If the light goes off, the issue is resolved. If the light stays on, the DPF needs professional cleaning. If the car goes into limp mode, stop driving — professional clean required. What's the difference between DPF cleaning and regeneration? + Regeneration is the normal process of burning off soot (happens during driving). Forced regeneration is done by a specialist using diagnostic equipment (£85-£300). Professional cleaning is a physical cleaning process (off-car or on-car) (£150-£400). Cleaning is more effective for severe clogging. How often should I clean my DPF? + Most vehicles need DPF cleaning every 30,000-40,000 miles , or when the DPF warning light appears. Regular long journeys (40mph+ for 20 mins) prevent clogging. If you only do short journeys, more frequent cleaning may be needed. Can I remove the DPF to save money? + NO — DPF removal is illegal. It will cause your vehicle to fail the MOT, you may be fined (£1,000+), and your insurance will be void. Avoid any garage offering DPF delete/"gut" services — it's illegal and will cause you serious problems. Why do DPFs fail? + Short journeys (DPF can't regenerate), faulty EGR valve (more soot), faulty injectors (more soot), oil ash accumulation, faulty sensors (ECU doesn't regenerate), and low engine oil level. Short journeys are the most common cause. Is DPF cleaning guaranteed to work? + In most cases (90%+), professional off-car cleaning resolves the issue. However, if the DPF is cracked, melted, or structurally damaged, cleaning won't work and replacement is needed. A specialist will inspect and advise. How long does DPF cleaning take? + Off-car cleaning takes 1-2 days (vehicle off the road). Forced regeneration takes a few hours (vehicle may be drivable within hours). Replacement takes 2-3 days . Postal cleaning takes 3-5 days . Can I clean a DPF myself? + No — professional cleaning requires specialist equipment (cleaning machine, high-pressure water, air). DIY cleaning methods (chemicals, pressure washing) are not effective and can damage the DPF. Use a specialist. Does DPF cleaning affect performance? + Yes — a clean DPF restores performance. After cleaning, you'll notice: restored power, improved fuel economy, smoother engine running, no DPF warning light, and no smoke. How long does a DPF last? + A DPF should last 100,000+ miles with regular maintenance. However, DPFs can fail earlier due to short journeys, faulty components (EGR, injectors), or poor maintenance. Regular cleaning extends DPF life. Does DPF replacement affect insurance? + Any major mechanical work, including DPF replacement, should be declared to your insurer. The work may affect vehicle value and should be recorded. DPF removal (illegal) will void your insurance. Before you agree

sections.heading: 10 Questions to Ask Before DPF Service

blocks.text: Asking the right questions can save you hundreds and prevent unnecessary replacement. Here's a checklist specific to DPF issues.
1. Is cleaning possible or do I need replacement?
In most cases, cleaning resolves the issue. Replacement is only needed if cracked, melted, or severely damaged.
2. What's included in the cleaning price?
Get a full written breakdown: removal, cleaning, refitting, testing, and diagnostic reset.
3. What cleaning method do you use?
Off-car cleaning (best), forced regeneration (mild issues), or chemical (less effective).
4. What's the condition of my DPF?
Ask for an inspection report. Is it clogged with soot, ash, or physically damaged?
5. What warranty do you offer on the cleaning?
Typical warranty is 6–12 months on the cleaning work. Get it in writing.
6. What's the root cause of the DPF issue?
Short journeys, faulty EGR, faulty injectors, or something else? Address the root cause.
7. What's the timeline from booking to completion?
Off-car cleaning: 1-2 days. Forced regeneration: a few hours. Replacement: 2-3 days.
8. Is there any diagnostic work included?
Ask if fault code reading and DPF pressure measurement are included in the price.
9. Do you have experience with my vehicle/engine type?
Some engines have known DPF issues. Ask about their experience.
10. Can you provide a written quote?
Get everything in writing: scope of work, cost, timeline, and warranty terms.

cards.title: £800 to £3,500+
cards.text: How much does DPF replacement cost in the UK? + DPF replacement costs range from £800 to £3,500+ depending on vehicle. Compact cars cost £800-£1,500, family cars £1,500-£2,500, and SUVs/commercial vehicles £2,500-£3,500+. However, cleaning (£150-£400) resolves most issues — replacement is only needed when the filter is physically cracked or melted.

cards.text: Can I clean a DPF instead of replacing it? + Yes — in most cases, cleaning resolves the issue. Off-car professional cleaning (£180-£400) restores the filter to near-new condition. cards.text: What are the signs of a clogged DPF? + DPF warning light, reduced power / limp mode, increased fuel consumption, excessive black smoke, rough idle, engine management light, and frequent regeneration. The DPF warning light is the most common early sign.
cards.fullText: What are the signs of a clogged DPF? + DPF warning light, reduced power / limp mode, increased fuel consumption, excessive black smoke, rough idle, engine management light, and frequent regeneration. The DPF warning light is the most common early sign.

cards.title: 40mph+ for 15-20 minutes
cards.text: Can I drive with a DPF warning light? + If the DPF warning light is on, drive at 40mph+ for 15-20 minutes to allow the filter to regenerate. If the light goes off, the issue is resolved. If the light stays on, the DPF needs professional cleaning. If the car goes into limp mode, stop driving — professional clean required.

cards.title: Regeneration
cards.text: What's the difference between DPF cleaning and regeneration? + Regeneration is the normal process of burning off soot (happens during driving). Forced regeneration is done by a specialist using diagnostic equipment (£85-£300). Professional cleaning is a physical cleaning process (off-car or on-car) (£150-£400). Cleaning is more effective for severe clogging.

cards.title: 30,000-40,000 miles
cards.text: How often should I clean my DPF? + Most vehicles need DPF cleaning every 30,000-40,000 miles , or when the DPF warning light appears. Regular long journeys (40mph+ for 20 mins) prevent clogging. If you only do short journeys, more frequent cleaning may be needed.

cards.text: Can I remove the DPF to save money? + NO — DPF removal is illegal. It will cause your vehicle to fail the MOT, you may be fined (£1,000+), and your insurance will be void. Avoid any garage offering DPF delete/"gut" services — it's illegal and will cause you serious problems.

cards.title: Short journeys are the most common cause.
cards.text: Why do DPFs fail? + Short journeys (DPF can't regenerate), faulty EGR valve (more soot), faulty injectors (more soot), oil ash accumulation, faulty sensors (ECU doesn't regenerate), and low engine oil level. Short journeys are the most common cause.

cards.text: Is DPF cleaning guaranteed to work? + In most cases (90%+), professional off-car cleaning resolves the issue. However, if the DPF is cracked, melted, or structurally damaged, cleaning won't work and replacement is needed. A specialist will inspect and advise.

cards.title: 1-2 days
cards.text: How long does DPF cleaning take? + Off-car cleaning takes 1-2 days (vehicle off the road). Forced regeneration takes a few hours (vehicle may be drivable within hours). Replacement takes 2-3 days . Postal cleaning takes 3-5 days .

cards.title: Use a specialist.
cards.text: Can I clean a DPF myself? + No — professional cleaning requires specialist equipment (cleaning machine, high-pressure water, air). DIY cleaning methods (chemicals, pressure washing) are not effective and can damage the DPF. Use a specialist.

cards.text: Does DPF cleaning affect performance? + Yes — a clean DPF restores performance. After cleaning, you'll notice: restored power, improved fuel economy, smoother engine running, no DPF warning light, and no smoke.

cards.title: 100,000+ miles
cards.text: How long does a DPF last? + A DPF should last 100,000+ miles with regular maintenance. However, DPFs can fail earlier due to short journeys, faulty components (EGR, injectors), or poor maintenance. Regular cleaning extends DPF life.
